newsitem.title: UK: Med Urals firmer, headed towards Dated Brent parit.
newsitem.headline: Med Urals firmer, headed towards Dated Brent parit.

text.p: Prices for Russian Urals sour crude in the Mediterranean continued to firm on Monday with mid-December cargoes offered as high as Dated Brent parity, traders said.
"We're looking for Dated flat," said a trader with a Urals cargo loading Dec 12-13.
End-November cargoes traded two weeks ago at Dated Brent -70 cents.
Bids hovered around Dated Brent -20, with buyers complaining that sellers were holding vessels back.
"Sellers are keeping vessels, they're not showing them," said one Italian refiner.
Nevertheless, traders agreed that the Mediterranean market was fundamentally tight with North sea grades apparently now too expensive to move to the Med.
"With the freight rate and the premium on Dated Brent it has become too expensive (to move Forties and Oseberg to the Med)," said the Italian refiner.
Traders said Urals prices were underpinned by loading delays at the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.

Berth number one, the only berth at the port which can accommodate cargoes of between 100,000 and 140,000 tonnes was closed on Monday due to a heavy swell. The berth is scheduled to close again on Dec 9-24 for maintenance.
"Urals certainly isn't going to lose any of its tightness," said one trader.
But some dealers said that Iraqi exports, expected soon under the U.N. oil-for-food plan, would loosen up the sour crude market and should put pressure on Urals prices.

An Iraqi newspaper on Monday quoted Foreign Minister Saeed al-Sahaf as saying that Iraq had already started signing sales contracts with international oil firms within the framework of the limited oil sales plan.

Iraq has priced its Kirkuk export grade at Dated Brent -$1.55 a barrel for European lifters. Some European refiners said the price was too high, but some key market players expressed satisfaction with the price, given current high Urals quotes.
